assumedContext: Session network egress is blocked for all domains except the search index; WebFetch returns EGRESS_BLOCKED and curl reports CONNECT 403 against data.sec.gov, fred.stlouisfed.org and stockanalysis.com. Figures sourced to Meta filings reached this analysis via search-index summaries of those filings, not the documents themselves.
Phases 2-5 not yet run at time of writing; capex and balance-sheet figures cited here are carried forward and re-derived in Phase 4.

findings.claim: Q2 2026 advertising revenue growth decomposes exactly into impressions +14% and price per ad +12% ((1.14 x 1.12) - 1 = +27.7% vs +27% reported), on Family daily active people of 3.60bn, up only 3% y/y.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Meta Q2 2026 results, 8-K exhibit 99.1 filed 2026-07-29 (via search-index summary)

findings.claim: Q2 2026 revenue rose 28% to $60.80bn while total costs and expenses rose 55%; operating margin fell from 43% to 31%.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Meta Q2 2026 results, 8-K exhibit 99.1 filed 2026-07-29; CNBC 2026-07-29

findings.claim: Europe delivered the fastest price-per-ad growth of any region at +19% y/y, despite being the jurisdiction with the most restrictive data-combination regime (DMA).
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Meta Q2 2026 earnings presentation (via search-index summary), 2026-07-29

findings.claim: In FTC v. Meta the court held the FTC failed to prove Meta currently holds monopoly power in personal social networking; no divestiture of Instagram or WhatsApp. The reasoning rested on finding real competition from TikTok and YouTube.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE
findings.source: US District Court for the District of Columbia (Boasberg J.), decision 2025-11-18; Sullivan & Cromwell client memo; NPR and CNBC reporting

findings.claim: Meta agreed a youth-safety settlement with 47-52 state attorneys general reported at $16.7-18bn, payable annually over 10 years, with 30% of the sum released only if YouTube and TikTok adopt equivalent design measures (one-hour daily limit, nighttime block, age assurance).
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE
findings.source: CNBC ($16.7bn), NPR and PBS ($17bn), Variety ('up to $18bn'), all 2026-08-26; trial before Gonzalez Rogers J., N.D. Cal.

findings.claim: Meta booked a $2.4bn charge for legal proceedings in Q2 2026 G&A, before the August state AG settlement was agreed - so the settlement is not fully provisioned in the 2026-06-30 balance sheet.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: The European Commission fined Meta EUR 200m for DMA non-compliance over the pay-or-consent model and required a genuine less-personalised alternative; Meta rolled the less-personalised option out more broadly into 2026.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE
findings.source: European Commission DMA non-compliance decision, 2025-04-22; EU Perspectives 2026-03

findings.claim: Mark Zuckerberg holds 99.7% of Class B stock (10 votes per share), equating to roughly 13% of economics and approximately 61% of voting power. Meta is a controlled company; no minority mechanism can alter capital allocation.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Meta proxy materials and shareholder proposal filings; Harvard Law CorpGov Forum; Public Citizen analysis

findings.claim: Meta repurchased zero Class A shares in the six months to 2026-06-30 with $25.03bn of authorisation unused, while paying a $0.525/quarter dividend ($1.353bn in Q2) against Q2 free cash flow of $0.784bn - the dividend was funded with debt.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: OpenAI launched advertising in ChatGPT on 2026-02-09 and a self-serve Ads Manager, reaching roughly $1bn annualised ad revenue run-rate from about $100m six months earlier; the TikTok US joint venture closed with roughly 80% non-Chinese ownership, removing TikTok's regulatory overhang with US advertisers.
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: USD m annualised OpenAI ad run-rate
findings.source: Axios 2026-04-09 and 2026-05-05; Benzinga 2026-08; Marketing Dive on TikTok US JV NewFront, 2026

findings.claim: Meta trades at 19.4x consensus 2026 EPS of $31.72 and 18.2x consensus 2027 EPS of $33.89 at $615.20, versus Alphabet at roughly 16.8-17.0x, Microsoft 26.7x, Apple 36.1x, Netflix 31.2x and Oracle 25.0x; the shares are down about 15% over twelve months against a 52-week range of $520.26-$790.80.
findings.label: CONSENSUS
findings.source: stockanalysis.com and TipRanks consensus aggregates; fullratio, financecharts, macrotrends and public.com peer P/E pages, retrieved 2026-09-06

findings.claim: Cost of equity derived at 10.0%: risk-free 4.79% (US 10-year Treasury, 2026-09-04) plus beta 1.15 times an equity risk premium of 4.5%.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived. Risk-free from US 10-year Treasury yield 4.79% reported 2026-09-04 (CNBC/TradingEconomics); beta and ERP are analyst assumptions stated in Phase 1 section 1.4

risks.text: Pricing power is engineered, not contractual: the 12% price-per-ad gain must be re-bought each year with compute, so the cost of maintaining price rises with the price itself
Design mandates from the youth-safety settlement act on impressions rather than price - the first regulatory instrument to attack the volume term of Meta's revenue identity
Controlled-company structure leaves minorities with no mechanism to influence a capital programme now running at $130-145bn a year
Antitrust victory rested on a finding of real competition from TikTok and YouTube; TikTok's US JV and OpenAI's ad platform make that finding more accurate every quarter

catalysts.text: Q3 2026 results: incremental charge for the state AG settlement, first full quarter of the design mandates, and the first 2027 capex signal
Meta discloses 2027 capital expenditure guidance - the single largest driver of the equity value
European Commission assessment of whether the less-personalised ads option satisfies the DMA remedy
Resumption of share repurchases against the $25.03bn unused authorisation - the clearest signal that the capex peak has passed

conclusions: All of Meta's growth is price times impressions on a flat user base: Family DAP +3% while impressions rose 14% and price per ad 12%. The revenue identity closes exactly. This is an intensity story, not a reach story.
The price-setting mechanism is a machine-learning system, not a contract or a tariff. It must be re-purchased annually with compute, which makes Phase 4's capex the direct input to Phase 1's price.

The structural legal risk was removed in November 2025 with the FTC verdict and replaced in August 2026 by a $16.7-18bn youth-safety settlement whose design mandates attack impressions rather than price.

Meta is a controlled company: 61% of votes in one hand, buybacks suspended, dividend funded with debt, capex guidance raised twice in 2026. There is no minority mechanism and therefore no governance catalyst to close the discount.
Europe prices fastest of any region (+19% per ad) under the heaviest data regulation - the most counter-consensus fact in this phase and unexplained on public disclosure.

Structural discount assessment: Meta's 18.2x 2027 consensus P/E versus the mega-cap set is a governance-plus-capex-uncertainty discount that no governance event can dissolve. It closes only through demonstrated returns on the capital programme.
thesisImpact: Reframes the company from 'cheap mega-cap with an AI option' to 'an auction whose clearing price is a function of compute spend, run by a controlling shareholder who has suspended shareholders' claim on cash while that spend runs'. Every later phase tests one question: does the compute buy more price than it costs?
